controls.name: mode
controls.doc: The side of the threshold the band acts on. Above acts when the band is loud, taming a resonance that only rings when pushed; below acts when it is quiet, lifting a band that drops out. The order is the integer the kernel reads: above is 0, below is 1.

controls.name: threshold
controls.doc: Where the band starts to act, in dB of the band's own level and not the strip's. It is the same fact the de-esser's threshold is, so it carries the same travel.

controls.name: ratio
controls.doc: How hard the band is held once it is past its threshold. 2:1 rather than the de-esser's 4:1, because a dynamic band is corrective, not a limiter for a sibilant.

controls.name: range
controls.doc: The most the band may add to its static gain, signed: below zero the deepest cut, above zero the largest boost. The ceiling of +12 keeps static plus dynamic inside the EQ's own travel. Zero makes the band inert without switching it off.

controls.name: attack
controls.doc: The detector's attack, in ms. The travel stops at the oversampling floor, below which the band would need the compressor's delayed control path.

controls.name: release
controls.doc: The detector's release, in ms. 100 ms is long enough not to modulate a 40 Hz band inside four cycles.

BAND_DYN_KNEE_DB.doc: The soft knee of the band's gain computer, in dB. One knee for the one band-dynamics word, shared by every stage that runs it, the de-esser included: a second spelling of 6 would be a second place where the reduction starts.

BAND_DYN_MAX_BANDS.doc: How many dynamic bands a channel may hold. A dynamic band is an operator band, so the capacity is the operator's reserve, read and not typed again.

DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_AUTO_MS.doc: The shortest attack, in ms, at which the compressor's detector does not alias. Below it the compressor engages its 4x control path, which adds 72 samples of latency; a zero-latency band has no such path, so its attack travel stops at this floor.
